title: Mozilla, Google, Apple block compromised eMudhra CA certificates
content_md: Certificate authority eMudhra revoked eight compromised intermediate certificates after researchers found their private keys were so weak that anyone could recover them almost instantly and use them to forge trusted certificates for legitimate websites. Major browsers and operating systems trusted the compromised certificates, potentially allowing attackers to impersonate legitimate websites and intercept encrypted communications. A security researcher known as Wayne discovered the weakness on October 17 while scanning publicly available certificate data. According to Mozilla's incident report , all eight certificates used P-384 private keys generated in April 2025 that had values smaller than 256, allowing anyone to recover them by testing just 256 possible numbers. To demonstrate the weakness, security researcher Flüpke published one of the compromised private keys on GitHub , showing that the private key for eMudhra's "EM OV TLS CA - G3C" certificate had a value of just 4. BleepingComputer independently verified that the published key matches one of the revoked certificates. In a response to Mozilla , eMudhra blamed the issue on an error in a script used to generate the certificates in April 2025. The company said the error generated a second set of weaker keys that were mistakenly selected for certificate signing because they had labels similar to the properly generated keys. Some of the resulting certificates were also submitted to Sectigo for cross-signing. eMudhra said
